cache.description: Re-creatable files kept between runs, such as a downloaded Chrome.

departures.description: Departure boards shown on the display, in order. Each picks its own provider.

limits.description: How long a render, and each source in it, may take.

providers.description: Credentials and endpoints shared by all boards using a provider.

schedule.description: When to refresh. Left out, the program renders once and exits unless `--cron` or `--every` say otherwise.

server.description: Serves the rendered image to displays that fetch it, like the reTerminal E1003.

stale_data.description: How long an earlier result stands in for a source that has failed.

AdminConfig.description:
The admin interface: how the owner of a running server looks at it and changes it (opening the pairing window,
and later approving displays), from the same machine, with `displayctl`. It is a local socket, not a network
port. It runs only when HTTPS does (`transport = "prefer-https"` or `"https"`), because pairing is what it is for.

enabled.description:
Offer the admin interface. Turn it off and nothing can open the pairing window, so no new display can join
until it is back on.

socket.description:
Where the socket is. Left out, it is `admin.sock` in `[server.tls] directory`. A Unix socket path has to be
short (about 100 bytes), and the directory it is in has to be closed to other users; set this if either is
a problem for the default.

CacheConfig.description: Where files that can be re-created (a downloaded Chrome, for one) are kept between runs.

directory.description: Relative paths are resolved against the working directory.

DepartureBoardConfig.description: One `[[departures]]` entry: a titled board fed by a single provider.

enabled.description: Set to false to skip this board without deleting it.

name.description: Heading shown above the board on the display.

rows.description: Maximum number of rows to show.

travel_minutes.description:
Minutes it takes to get to the station or stop. Services leaving sooner than
this are left off, since they can't be caught. National Rail boards support up to 119.

oneOf.description: National Rail live board between two CRS codes.

from.description: CRS code of the station to show departures from, e.g. "HRN".

to.description: CRS code the services must call at, e.g. "WIH".

oneOf.description: TfL arrivals at a single stop (bus stop or station NaPTAN id).

dither.description: How greys are reduced to the panel's levels.

image_format.description:
The format the reTerminal E1003 is sent when it has no preference. Every format is published, and the
display can ask for another with its `Accept` header. Ignored by displays driven directly.

kind.description: Which display to render for and drive. Its size and colour depth are fixed by the hardware.

oneOf.description: Seeed reTerminal E1003, 10.3" 1872x1404 with 16 greys. Fetches its image from the `[server]`.

Dither.description: How to reduce the rendered image to fewer levels.

oneOf.description: Plain threshold: crisp text, harsh on greys.
Error diffusion: smooth greys, a bit noisy on text.
4x4 Bayer matrix: regular pattern, stable between refreshes.

save_directory.description: Where rendered images are saved; empty for the working directory.

ImageFormat.description: The file format the reTerminal E1003 downloads.

oneOf.description: 8-bit greyscale, uncompressed (about 2.6 MB). The simplest for the firmware to decode.
8-bit greyscale, compressed (well under 200 KB). Less to download, but the firmware has to inflate it.
Lossless, a little larger than PNG (about 160 KB), but decoded in one cheap pass with no inflate step.

LimitsConfig.description: Time limits that keep one stuck part from stopping the dashboard updating.

render_deadline_seconds.description:
A whole run, from fetching to the display, is abandoned after this long. Leave room for the
sources' timeout plus Chrome (30 s, and a relaunch), and for a first-run Chrome download.

source_timeout_seconds.description: A source (the weather, or one departures board) that hasn't answered by then counts as failed.

latitude.description: Decimal degrees, used for the weather lookup.

timezone.description:
The IANA timezone the display is in, e.g. `Europe/London` or `America/New_York`. The refresh schedule's hours
and weekdays, the clock and date on the dashboard, and the day boundaries are all in this zone. Left out, the
host's own zone is used and a warning is logged: a container or cloud machine is usually UTC, which is
wrong wherever the display is, so set it.

api_key.description: Consumer Key from your raildata.org.uk "Live Arrival and Departure Boards" subscription.

host_url.description: Base path up to and including the operation name; the CRS code is appended as the final path segment.

air_quality_host_url.description: Air quality is served from its own host.

host_url.description: Open-Meteo API base URL, e.g. for a self-hosted instance or a paid plan.

pollen.description: Also fetch pollen counts (Europe only). Off by default; they are not shown on the display yet.

ProvidersConfig.description: Credentials/endpoints shared by every board using that provider, under `[providers.*]`.

cron.description:
Cron expressions in local time (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week), e.g. `*/10 * * * *`.
A refresh is due whenever any of them is, so each can cover its own hours and days. For example, every
minute on weekday mornings, every 15 minutes the rest of the time on weekdays, and hourly at weekends:
`["* 7-8 * * 1-5", "*/15 * * * 1-5", "0 8-21 * * 6,0"]`. The start-up log says what they mean in words
and how many refreshes each day gets; each one is a wake of the display, which is what drains its battery.

ServerConfig.description: The HTTP server that hands the latest rendered image to displays that fetch it.

admin.description: How the owner looks at the running server and changes it. See `AdminConfig`.

advertise.description: Announce the server over mDNS / DNS-SD so it shows up in a scan of the network.

bind.description:
Address to listen on. The image is served at `/image`, with no authentication, so keep it on the LAN.
`[::]:8080` takes IPv4 and IPv6 clients on one socket, and the server announces both over mDNS; a host
without IPv6 falls back to IPv4. `0.0.0.0:8080` is IPv4 only, and `[::]` with a specific address is that
address only.

device_overdue_grace_seconds.description:
A display is reported overdue (`/status`, `/metrics`) once it is this much later than the
time it was told to return at. Covers a slow Wi-Fi join; a flat battery far exceeds it.

directory.description: Where the image to serve is written. Relative paths are resolved against the working directory.

instance_name.description: The name shown for the service in a scan, at most 63 bytes. The host name `<name>.local` is derived from it.

refresh_cooldown_seconds.description:
The display's button asks for a render with `POST /refresh`. Requests are refused (and the
current image returned) when a render started within this many seconds.

stale_grace_seconds.description: How late a scheduled render may be before the image is reported stale.

transport.description:
Plain HTTP, HTTPS, or both: `"http"`, `"prefer-https"` or `"https"`. See `[server.tls]` for the
HTTPS side. The default is `"http"`, so a configuration without this behaves as it always has.

wake_delay_seconds.description:
How long after a scheduled render the display is told to come back, so the new image is ready.
Also how soon it retries while a render is due but not finished.

StaleDataConfig.description:
When a source fails, the dashboard shows what it said last time, labelled with its age, until it
is older than this; after that the part is shown as unavailable.

departures_max_age_minutes.description: Departures go out of date quickly, so this is short.

app_key.description: Optional: anonymous requests work but are rate limited.

TlsConfig.description: HTTPS and the certificate authority behind it. Used when `transport` is `prefer-https` or `https`.

bind.description: Address for HTTPS. Must differ from `bind`'s port when both run (`prefer-https`).

device_certificate_days.description:
How long a display's certificate lasts, from 1 to 3650 days. Short on purpose: a display renews it with a third of its life
left, so renewal happens all the time and not once in years when no one remembers how it works, and a
display that has stopped renewing shows in `/status` within weeks. It is not what keeps a revoked
display out (that takes effect on its next request). A display that is off for longer than this gets
a new certificate by itself, with no one at the server, when it is next switched on.

directory.description:
Where the server's certificate authority and the list of displays that have joined are kept.
Back this directory up: its `authority.key` is the one thing that can't be remade without
pairing every display again. Relative paths are resolved against the working directory.

names.description:
More host names and IP addresses for the server's certificate, for a browser or `curl` to connect
by. Left empty, it is `<instance_name>.local` (the name announced over mDNS, with the characters a
host name can't have replaced) and `localhost`. The certificate also always has the fixed name
`home-display.internal`, which is what a display checks, so changing this never affects them.

pairing_retry_minutes.description: How long a display that is waiting for approval is told to wait before asking again, from 1 to 1440 minutes.

require_channel_binding.description:
Require a request for a certificate to prove it was made on the connection it arrived on
(RFC 9266). Leave off until the displays do this.

server_certificate_days.description: How long the server's own certificate lasts, from 1 to 3650 days. It is replaced when a third of that is left.

Transport.description:
How displays reach the server.

`http` is plain HTTP, as before: nothing is encrypted and anyone on the network can read the
picture or pose as the server. `prefer-https` serves both: a display that has joined uses HTTPS and is
recognised by its certificate, and one that hasn't carries on over HTTP. That keeps every display
working while they are moved over, and protects against someone listening, but not against someone
who can interfere with the network, who can still send a display to HTTP. `https` serves HTTPS only
and only to displays that have joined: the one setting that protects against that. A display's own
setting (in its firmware) matters as much, since only a display set to HTTPS-only is certain not to
fall back.

enabled.description: When false no weather is fetched and the display shows none.

open_meteo.description: Optional: Open-Meteo needs no key, so the default host is used when omitted.

oneOf.description: Needs an API key and a One Call by Call subscription for the 4.0 API.
Free for non-commercial use, no key.
